decision.about: whether the card’s ask mechanism (yes/no, or option cards) and its verdict mechanism (Approve/Improve) should be one control or stay two

options.say: keep ask and verdict as two separate, differently-shaped controls on the same card -- ask_controls() for a direct yes/no question the mastermind is asking, verdict_controls() for the owner judging a finished report
options.why: they answer two different questions and already read that way on screen: an ask is short-lived and specific ("restart the server?"), a verdict is the owner’s standing judgement on a piece of finished work, complete with undo and a note. Folding them into one shape would either force every ask to carry Approve/Improve’s own undo-and-note baggage, or strip the verdict of what makes it a verdict.

options.say: build one combined control that renders as buttons either way, reading its own options off whichever field the card carries
options.why: fewer functions, and "yes/no" versus "approve/improve" are close enough in shape (both are just labelled buttons) that a reader might expect one mechanism

decision.because: this matches the brief’s own read, which this task is not overturning: an ask is the mastermind asking the owner something, a verdict is the owner judging something the mastermind already finished -- different directions, different lifetimes (an ask is answered once and done; a verdict can be undone, changed, and re-approved). The two controls already coexist cleanly on one card (detail() renders ask_controls() when c.ask is set and verdict_controls() when the card is eligible -- both can appear on the same card, in order, and neither one’s label or behaviour needed to change for the other to exist). The real problem this task found was not that the two were confusing each other -- the owner never mentioned ask at all -- it was that Approve/Improve’s own labels did not say what they do and the reader could not reliably even reach them (the click-through bug). Both are now fixed without touching the verdict model.

assign.outcome:
**Approve and Improve now say what they'll do, show what happened, and actually reach the owner from wherever they're browsing.** The real bug behind "I don't know what this button does" was mostly that a card's own url did not reliably open its own detail — landing there while the toolbar's saved view read "grid" or "now" silently redrew the same wall instead, url changed, nothing else did. Fixed: a card's own url now always shows that card, with a plain sentence above Approve/Improve saying what each does, and a toast (with Undo) confirming a press actually did something, surviving the automatic move to the next card. Of the owner's four spacing/colour complaints, two were already fixed by this morning's `ai-padding` task (sub-card padding, link-blue titles — both traced to a missing `.card` class, now restored) and two needed a real fix here: `.v3-verdict`/`.v3-ask-block` hardcoded `1em` instead of the card's own default `--gap` rhythm, so the last section of a card's detail sat visibly closer than everywhere else — removed, the card's own default now reaches it, matching the owner's own words: "just add the default gap." Proven end to end (press, toast, undo, improve-with-a-note landing in the mastermind's own inbox) against a scratch board+verdicts pair in this task's own folder — the real `board.jsonl`/`verdicts.jsonl` are hashed before and after and byte-identical. One decision made and logged: ask and verdict stay two separate controls, not merged.

Left, on purpose: no readme/doc/ added to `ai/v/3` — same call inbox-zero made yesterday, the module still has none and every mechanism is documented in place in code. The pre-existing DOM-duplication on this page (several matches for `.v3-detail`/`.v3-split`, a hidden leftover route) is not new and not touched — it only mattered here as a measurement trap, worked around in every proof script.
